script.title: How a rover filmed its own landing on Mars
script.description: On 18 February 2021, NASA's Perseverance rover descended through the Martian atmosphere with onboard cameras recording every stage. This is the real footage of a one-ton machine touching down in Jezero Crater.
script.hook_card: Filming a landing on another world

shots.narration: Cameras on the spacecraft filmed the landing of this rover on the surface of Mars.
Perseverance hit the top of the atmosphere at about twenty thousand kilometres per hour.
A 21.5-metre parachute opened while the craft was supersonic, its pattern spelling Dare Mighty Things in binary.
Radio signals took about eleven minutes to reach Earth, so the landing was already over before mission control heard anything.
Cameras on the rocket-powered descent stage recorded the approach toward the surface of Jezero Crater.
The descent stage lowered the rover on 7.6-metre cables, then flew off to crash a safe distance away.
The rover landed in Jezero Crater, the site of a lake and river delta billions of years ago.
Cameras on the back shell, descent stage, and rover filmed a planetary landing for the first time.
